rationale: The land returns as the active player untaps their permanents in the untap step (502.3), so by the time the upkeep would begin the hand isn't empty; 614.10 states a skip is a replacement effect checked as the step would start and that a step already started can no longer be skipped.

Devour and Containment Priest are two replacement effects modifying the same enters-the-battlefield event: 616.1 has the affected object's controller choose one to apply, and 616.1f repeats the process with the effects that are now applicable, so choosing devour first doesn't actually remove the Priest; 702.82a defines devour as sacrificing as the object enters.

Same replacement-effect ordering machinery: 616.1 lets the controller pick the order, 616.1f repeats the process so Master Biomancer's effect is still applicable after devour is applied, and 702.82a gives the devour counter count.
601.2c states targets are announced during the casting process, well before costs are paid, so the mana actually spent doesn't affect whether a target is chosen.

514.1 is the discard-to-hand-size turn-based action and 514.2 is the later step where 'until end of turn'/'this turn' effects end, so the discard happens first; 723.1 (control lasts the entire turn) and 723.5 (the controller makes all that player's choices) each establish that Nola makes the discard choices.

514.2 lists what actually ends in the cleanup step; 723.1/723.5 state that the player-control effect lasts the whole turn and that the controller makes the controlled player's choices; 603.3b is the rule that a player orders the triggered abilities they control on the stack.
514.3a states that if a triggered ability is waiting during the cleanup step it goes on the stack, players get priority, and once the stack empties another cleanup step begins.
514.3a is why a player can get priority in that cleanup step at all; 514.2 defines the only effects that end there, so a restriction lasting the turn is still in force when priority is received.

500.8 states extra phases are added into the turn's structure directly after the specified phase (so the extra combat exists as a scheduled phase), and 724.1d states that ending the turn skips straight to the cleanup step, skipping every phase and step in between.
500.8 states extra phases are added directly after a specified phase; cast in an end step there is no 'this main phase' to append to, so no phase is created.
500.8 states the added phase goes directly after the specified phase, so a combat phase is created after the main phase the spell was cast in, i.e. the active player's own postcombat main phase.
Either rule independently states that unspent mana empties from a player's mana pool at the end of each step and phase, so the mana is gone once the draw step ends.
514.3 states that normally no player receives priority during the cleanup step, so no spells can be cast.

514.3a gives priority in this cleanup step because a discard trigger went on the stack; 514.2 lists what ends in the cleanup step, and a once-each-turn activation restriction isn't one of those, so it still applies.

702.94a defines miracle as revealing on the draw plus a triggered ability that lets you cast the card; 603.3 states the triggered ability isn't put on the stack until a player would next receive priority, i.e. after the spell finishes resolving, by which time the card has been discarded.

603.7/603.7b establish that the Guildmage creates a delayed triggered ability that waits for its trigger event (with a stated 'this turn' duration) rather than a continuous effect; 514.2 lists what actually ends in the cleanup step.

608.2h states that when an effect needs information about an object that is no longer in the zone it was expected to be in, its last known information is used, which is how Dracoplasm sees the sacrificed Myr as a 2/2.
The answer rests entirely on card text (Grafdigger's Cage names graveyards and libraries, Living Death puts the cards onto the battlefield from exile); no Comprehensive Rules chunk states this.
118.7a states that effects reducing a cost by an amount of generic mana affect only the generic component and can't touch colored or colorless components.

Either rule supports the distinction: 109.2 says a description using a card type without the word 'card' means a permanent on the battlefield, and 110.1 says a permanent is a card or token on the battlefield.
109.2 states that 'Rebels' with no zone specified and no word 'card' means Rebel permanents on the battlefield, so the effect doesn't reach a card being cycled from hand.

305.4 states that putting a land onto the battlefield isn't playing a land and doesn't count against the land drop; 118.6 and 202.1b each state that having no mana cost is an unpayable cost, so the 'pay its mana cost' option can't be taken.

201.5 states text referring to the object it's on by name means just that object, so the copied return-to-hand ability returns Mirage Mirror itself; 302.6 is the summoning sickness rule that keeps the returned Coral Eel from attacking.

712.9 states only permanents represented by double-faced cards/tokens can transform, which is why the physical Convicted Killer card can transform while the Recruiter's own ability transforms it; 707.2c states a static-ability copy effect fixes its copiable values when it first applies, so the transformed permanent is still a copy of the Recruiter's front face.

303.4f states an Aura entering from a zone other than the stack has its controller choose a legal object to enchant; 702.11b states hexproof only stops the permanent from being targeted, and no targeting occurs here.
208.3 states a noncreature permanent has no power or toughness, which is what breaks the 'power less than or equal to' condition once Mirage Mirror stops being a copy.

608.2c states the controller follows the spell's instructions in the order written, so the damage step happens before the life-gain step; 702.80a states wither-style damage puts -1/-1 counters on the creature instead of marking damage, which is what has already shrunk its toughness.
601.2d states that if a spell requires dividing or distributing an effect among targets, the division is announced as part of casting.

614.12 states that to determine which replacement effects apply as a permanent enters, you check its characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield, including its own static abilities, so Rusted Relic is a creature for Imposing Sovereign's effect.

614.12 states replacement effects are determined from the permanent's characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield (Nylea is a creature at that moment, so the enters-tapped effect applies); 603.2 states a triggered ability triggers when the game state matches its condition, and once Nylea is actually on the battlefield it isn't a creature.

608.2e states that for an action involving multiple players the choices are made in APNAP order and then the action is processed simultaneously, so both cards are put onto the battlefield at once; 614.12a states a choice required by an enters-the-battlefield replacement effect is made before the permanent enters.

The claim that 'the token' in the delayed exile clause covers every token the ability created is a card-specific ruling; no Comprehensive Rules chunk states how a singular token reference behaves when a replacement effect multiplies the tokens.

702.82a states devour sacrifices the creatures as the permanent enters (so the two events are simultaneous); 603.2 states the ability triggers when the game state matches its trigger event, which is checked after that event, with Feaster already on the battlefield.
The answer is about an effect that lets only one player ignore another effect; no Comprehensive Rules chunk states that such permission is player-specific, so this can't be traced to an inventory id.

701.3b states that attaching an Aura to the object it's already attached to does nothing; 603.2e states 'becomes attached' triggers only when the event actually happens and not if the state already exists.

103.5b states an action taken 'any time you could mulligan' happens when that player would declare a mulligan and that other players may already have made their declarations; 103.5 sets the turn order of those declarations.
702.62a defines suspend as a static ability functioning while the card is in a player's hand, exiling it from hand, so it can't be suspended off the top of the library.

704.3 states all applicable state-based actions are performed simultaneously as a single event; 704.5a/104.3b state a player at 0 or less life loses; 104.2a states the remaining player wins immediately once all opponents have left; 104.1 states the game ends immediately at that point, so no further SBA check happens.
400.7 states an object that changes zones becomes a new object with no relation to its previous existence, so the countered spell's card in the graveyard isn't the object the trigger refers to.

602.5c states that when an object acquires an activated ability with a use restriction from another object, that restriction applies to the acquired ability; 602.5b states such a restriction keeps applying regardless of who controls it.
Either rule states that restarting ends the current game and all players immediately begin a new game, so nothing from the old game carries over to the win condition.

701.21a states sacrificing moves the permanent from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard (so the dies trigger sees it); 903.9a states the commander move to the command zone happens later, as a state-based action.
601.2b states the value of X is announced during casting, after the card is already on the stack; 202.3e states X is treated as the chosen number while the object is on the stack and 0 elsewhere.
Both rules state the land-drop check is purely a count of lands played this turn versus lands the player may play, with no tie to any particular permanent.

111.7 and 704.5d each state a token outside the battlefield ceases to exist only as a state-based action, so it is briefly in the library; 111.8 states a token that has left the battlefield can't move to another zone, so it can't be put on the stack to be cast.

111.7 states the token goes to the graveyard and only ceases to exist as a state-based action; 111.8 states a token that has left the battlefield can't change zones; 702.52a defines dredge as returning the card from the graveyard to the hand, which the token can't do.

704.5a/104.3b state the player at 0 or less life loses as a state-based action; 800.4a states that when that player leaves the game all objects they own leave the game, which is the event the Demon's ability is evaluated against.

607.3 states that when one of a pair of linked abilities has exiled multiple cards (usually because it was copied), the other ability refers to each of those exiled cards; 707.10b states a copy of an ability has the same source, which is what keeps the copy linked to the land's play ability.

604.3 states characteristic-defining abilities function in all zones, so Maraxus's power is defined while it's on the stack; 601.2i states the spell becomes cast (and cast-triggers trigger) only after all casting steps, including paying costs, are complete.

701.25d states an ability that triggers on surveil triggers after the whole surveil process is complete, and 603.2 states a trigger is checked against the game state when its event occurs, at which point Blood Operative is already in the graveyard.
